The proposed derivation checks out.

**Setup.** Let a = Σ_{v∈S} x_v². Then Σ_{v∈S̄} x_v² = 1 − a. Because S is independent, every edge lies either between S and S̄ or inside S̄.

**Equation 1.** The Rayleigh quotient of the full vector gives λ = xᵀAx = 2W_{SS̄} + 2W_{S̄}, where W_{SS̄} and W_{S̄} are the sums of x_u x_v over S–S̄ edges and over edges inside S̄, respectively.

**Equation 2.** For v ∈ S, all neighbors of v lie in S̄, and λx_v = Σ_{u∼v} x_u. Multiplying by x_v and summing over S gives λa = Σ_{v∈S} x_v Σ_{u∼v} x_u = W_{SS̄}. So 2W_{SS̄} = 2λa.

**Definition of q.** The restricted Rayleigh quotient is q = x_{S̄}ᵀA x_{S̄} / (1 − a) = 2W_{S̄}/(1 − a). So 2W_{S̄} = q(1 − a).

**Solving.** Substituting into Equation 1 gives λ = 2λa + q(1 − a). Hence λ − q = a(2λ − q), so a = (λ − q)/(2λ − q).

Then
1/2 − a = [(2λ − q) − 2(λ − q)] / [2(2λ − q)] = q / [2(2λ − q)].

This matches the stated final answer.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
